userStories.title: Install and configure Supabase SDK for frontend and backend
userStories.description:
Install @supabase/supabase-js in both frontend (root) and backend/. Create Supabase client files with SUPABASE_URL + SUPABASE_ANON_KEY. Add SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY to backend only (never exposed to browser). Configure backend supabaseAdmin client using service role for privileged operations that must bypass RLS (worker, scheduler, webhooks). Add all new env vars to .env.example files.

## Context
- **Frontend client location**: Create `src/lib/supabase.ts` alongside existing `src/lib/apiFetch.ts`. Use `VITE_` prefix for env vars (Vite convention) — `import.meta.env.VITE_SUPABASE_URL` and `import.meta.env.VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. Never import or reference the service role key in frontend code.

- **Backend client location**: Create `backend/src/lib/supabase.ts` alongside existing lib modules (llm-client, sse-hub, direction-stack, etc.). Export both `supabaseAdmin` (service role — bypasses RLS for worker/scheduler/webhook operations) and `supabaseAnon` (anon key — respects RLS for user-facing API routes). Follow the existing module pattern in `backend/src/lib/`.

- **Graceful degradation when env vars missing**: Backend must start without Supabase env vars — log a warning at import time, defer actual client creation to first use or export a lazy getter. This matches the project constraint that auth middleware is globally disabled and Rorca is primarily a local tool. Do NOT crash on missing env vars.

- **TypeScript strict mode**: Project uses TypeScript 5.7 strict — no implicit `any`, no `@ts-ignore` without comment. Generate Supabase types or use the generic `SupabaseClient` type. The `supabase-js` v2 client is well-typed out of the box.

- **Env var files**: Backend uses `backend/.env` (see existing `DATABASE_URL`, `PORT`, `RORCA_AGENT` pattern). Root frontend uses `.env.local`. Add examples to `.env.example` / `.env.local.example` respectively. Never commit actual keys — only example placeholders.

- **Package installation**: Run `npm install @supabase/supabase-js` in both root (frontend) and `backend/` directories. Both have independent `package.json` files. Do not use workspace hoisting.

- **Security gotcha**: `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` must ONLY exist in `backend/.env.example`, never in root `.env.local.example`. The service role key bypasses all RLS policies — exposing it to the browser would be a critical security vulnerability.

- **Existing patterns to follow**: Backend lib modules typically export singletons or factory functions. See `backend/src/lib/llm-client.ts` for the pattern of env-var-driven configuration with fallback defaults. The `errors.ts` hierarchy (`AppError`, `ValidationError`) is available if you need to throw on misconfiguration at runtime.

userStories.title: Replace custom JWT middleware with Supabase RS256 verification
userStories.description:
Replace the self-built HS256 JWT middleware in backend/src/lib/auth.ts with Supabase RS256 JWT verification via supabaseAdmin.auth.getUser(token). Keep the LOCAL_ADMIN synthetic user fallback for when SUPABASE_URL is not configured (backward compat for local dev without Supabase). Update authRequired middleware to extract Bearer token, call getUser(), attach req.user = { id, email, supabaseId } with the Supabase auth.users UUID as req.user.id.

## Context
- **Auth middleware is globally disabled** (`server.ts` ~line 78, `app.use(authRequired)` commented out). This is intentional for local dev — do NOT re-enable globally. MU-002 updates the middleware implementation but the global bypass remains. Routes that explicitly call `authRequired` will use the new Supabase path.

- **Existing `req.user.id` contract is critical**: Many routes reference `req.user.id` (rate-limiter keys it as `userId:method:path`, WAL events, `pipeline_runs`, `story_comments`, `notification_subscriptions`, etc.). The switch from a local DB integer/UUID to a Supabase `auth.users` UUID means all downstream consumers must work with the new ID format. Since auth is globally bypassed and LOCAL_ADMIN fallback is preserved, existing local dev won't break — but verify the LOCAL_ADMIN `id` value is a valid UUID format (not an integer) to avoid type mismatches if auth is ever re-enabled per-route.

- **`supabaseAdmin` client**: MU-001 (dependency) creates `backend/src/lib/supabase.ts` with `createClient(SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY)`. Import from there. The service-role client bypasses RLS, which is correct for server-side token verification via `auth.getUser(token)`.

- **Remove `jsonwebtoken` + `bcrypt` from auth.ts only** — these packages may still be used by other files (e.g., `refresh_tokens` table logic in auth routes, password hashing in `POST /api/auth/register`). Grep for all `require('jsonwebtoken')` / `import.*jsonwebtoken` before removing the dependency from `package.json`. MU-002 scope is `auth.ts` middleware, not the full auth route handlers.

- **Backward compat guard pattern**: Check `process.env.SUPABASE_URL` at middleware load time, not per-request. If unset, short-circuit to LOCAL_ADMIN injection (same `req.user = { id, email }` shape). This keeps `npm run dev` working without any Supabase config — matches the project's "local single-user tool" philosophy.

- **No migration needed**: This story modifies middleware code only. The `users` table and `auth` routes are untouched. If a `supabase_id` column is needed on the `users` table, that belongs to a separate story (likely MU-003+). `req.user.id` should be the raw Supabase UUID string, not a DB lookup.

- **Rate limiter key format**: `rate-limiter.ts` keys requests as `userId:method:path`. The switch from whatever LOCAL_ADMIN id was (likely `'local-admin'` or `1`) to a Supabase UUID won't break anything since it's just a string key — but be aware that rate limit buckets will reset for authenticated users after this change.

userStories.title: Add auth_id column and get_user_workspace_ids() helper function
userStories.description:
Create a PostgreSQL migration (timestamp-prefixed) that: (1) adds auth_id UUID column to users table linking to Supabase auth.users.id; (2) creates the workspace_members table (the membership join table needed by all workspace-scoped RLS policies); (3) creates get_user_workspace_ids(p_auth_id UUID) SECURITY DEFINER function. This single migration must be done atomically because workspace_members must exist before get_user_workspace_ids() can be created, and both must exist before any workspace RLS policies (MU-010) are enabled. The migration must be non-destructive and idempotent.

## Context
- **Dependency order is critical**: workspace_members MUST be created in THIS migration (not MU-028) because MU-010 enables RLS on workspaces and calls get_user_workspace_ids() at runtime. MU-028 only adds the route-level INSERT into workspace_members — it does not create the table.

## Context
- **Migration naming**: Use timestamp format `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_add_auth_id_to_users.sql` in `backend/src/db/pg-migrations/`. Existing migrations are 001–079 sequential; new ones must be timestamp-prefixed (numeric sort puts them after existing ones). Check for duplicate prefixes — `pg-index.ts` runs `checkDuplicatePrefixes()` at startup and fails loudly on collisions.

- **`auth.users` FK requires Supabase schema**: The `REFERENCES auth.users(id)` foreign key assumes the `auth` schema exists in the database. This is a Supabase-managed schema — verify it's accessible from the migration context. If running locally without Supabase, the migration will fail on the FK constraint. Consider wrapping the FK in a conditional or documenting the Supabase dependency.

- **Idempotency pattern**: PostgreSQL natively supports `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`, and `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION`. Use all three — the migration runner (`pg-index.ts`) tracks applied migrations in `schema_migrations` (BIGINT version column) and runs each in a transaction, but idempotency is still good practice for manual re-runs.

- **SECURITY DEFINER ownership**: The function must be owned by a superuser role (typically `postgres`) for SECURITY DEFINER to bypass RLS. Add `ALTER FUNCTION get_user_workspace_ids(UUID) OWNER TO postgres;` explicitly after the CREATE. Also add `SET search_path = rorca, public` on the function definition to prevent search_path injection attacks (same class of issue as the AGE search_path poison bug).

- **Workspace membership join table**: Check whether `team_members` (existing table with `user_id` + team → workspace mapping) or a direct `workspace_members` table exists. The function needs to resolve `auth_id → user.id → workspace IDs`. Current schema has `teams` + `team_members` — the function may need to join `users → team_members → teams → workspaces` unless a simpler direct mapping exists.

- **Non-destructive for existing rows**: `auth_id` must be nullable (`UUID` without `NOT NULL`) so existing users aren't broken. The `UNIQUE` constraint allows NULLs in PostgreSQL (multiple rows can have `auth_id = NULL`). Don't add a `NOT NULL` constraint — users only get `auth_id` populated on first Supabase login.

- **Pool connection hygiene**: If this function will be called from application code via the `pg` pool, ensure the calling code uses `$1` parameterized queries (not string interpolation). The existing `query<T>(sql, params)` helper in `backend/src/db/index.ts` handles this correctly.
acceptanceCriteria: New migration file YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_add_auth_id_and_workspace_members.sql with correct timestamp prefix
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS auth_id UUID UNIQUE REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_auth_id ON users(auth_id)

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workspace_members (workspace_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES workspaces(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, user_auth_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('owner','admin','member')), joined_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), PRIMARY KEY (workspace_id, user_auth_id))
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workspace_members_user_auth_id ON workspace_members(user_auth_id)
SECURITY DEFINER function: get_user_workspace_ids(p_auth_id UUID) RETURNS TABLE(workspace_id TEXT) — queries workspace_members WHERE user_auth_id = p_auth_id
Function language is LANGUAGE plpgsql (not SQL) for lazy table resolution compatibility
Function body includes SET search_path = rorca, public to prevent search_path injection

Existing rows: auth_id stays NULL until user logs in via Supabase (non-destructive)
Migration runs cleanly on existing DB without data loss or column duplication

userStories.title: Replace AuthContext with Supabase session management
userStories.description:
Replace src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx's custom JWT/localStorage logic with Supabase Auth session management using supabase.auth.getSession(), supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange(), and supabase.auth.signOut(). Update apiFetch in src/lib/apiFetch.ts to read the Bearer token from the Supabase session access_token instead of localStorage.

## Context
- **Auth middleware is globally disabled** (`backend/src/server.ts` ~line 78, intentionally commented out). MU-004 replaces the client-side auth context only — do NOT re-enable server-side `authRequired` middleware as part of this story. Server-side Supabase JWT verification belongs to a separate story.

- **Existing AuthContext exports**: Check all consumers of `AuthContext` across `src/` before changing the shape. The current context likely exposes `user`, `token`, `login()`, `logout()`, `isAuthenticated`. The new shape drops `token` (now internal to Supabase session) and `login()` (handled by Supabase UI/redirect). Grep for `useAuth` to find every consumer and ensure none depend on removed fields.

- **apiFetch pattern** (`src/lib/apiFetch.ts`): Currently reads a token from `localStorage`. Replace with an async call to `supabase.auth.getSession()` — note this is async, so `apiFetch` may need to become async if it isn't already. Avoid caching the token in a module-level variable; always read from the Supabase session to pick up automatic refreshes.

- **Supabase client singleton**: MU-004 depends on a shared `supabase` client instance (likely created in MU-002 or MU-003 at `src/lib/supabase.ts`). Import from there — do NOT create a second client. Multiple GoTrueClient instances cause competing `onAuthStateChange` listeners and race conditions on token refresh.

- **`onAuthStateChange` cleanup**: The subscription returns an `{ data: { subscription } }` object. Call `subscription.unsubscribe()` in the `useEffect` cleanup to prevent memory leaks on unmount/HMR. Vite HMR with `@refresh reset` on context providers can cause duplicate subscriptions if cleanup is missed.

- **isLoading guard is critical**: The `isLoading=true` initial state prevents a flash where `isAuthenticated=false` causes redirects or blank screens before the session is restored. All route guards and conditional renders must check `isLoading` before acting on `isAuthenticated`.

- **TypeScript strict mode**: User type must be `import { User } from '@supabase/supabase-js'` — no custom user type or `any` cast. Session type is `Session | null`. The context value interface should be explicit (not inferred) for consumer type safety.

- **No manual token refresh logic**: Remove any existing `setInterval`-based token refresh or `/api/auth/refresh` calls. Supabase SDK handles refresh automatically via `onAuthStateChange` `TOKEN_REFRESHED` event. Leftover manual refresh would race with the SDK.

userStories.title: Build Login page with Supabase email+password auth
userStories.description:
Create src/pages/auth/LoginPage.tsx with email + password form. Calls supabase.auth.signInWithPassword(). After successful login, navigate to / (or ?returnTo= param). Show loading state during sign-in. Display error message on invalid credentials. Include 'Forgot password?' link to /auth/forgot-password and 'Create account' link to /auth/register. Add route /auth/login in App.tsx.

## Context
- **Supabase client import**: Use the shared Supabase client instance from the auth context/provider established in MU-003/MU-004 — do NOT create a new `createClient()` call. The `useAuth()` hook or context should expose `supabase` or a `signIn` method.

- **Route placement in App.tsx**: The `/auth/login` route MUST be outside the `RequireAuth` wrapper (per AC). Rorca uses `react-router-dom` v7 — check existing route structure in `App.tsx` for the pattern used by other public routes. Legacy panel IDs have `<Navigate>` redirects; follow that pattern.

- **`returnTo` param handling**: Use `useSearchParams()` to read `?returnTo=` and `useNavigate()` for redirect. Sanitize the `returnTo` value — only allow relative paths (no `https://evil.com` open redirect). Fallback to `/` if param is missing or invalid.

- **Dark theme consistency**: Rorca's UI uses `bg-gray-900`, `text-white`, Tailwind utility classes only (no custom CSS). Match existing panel styling — check `src/panels/` for color tokens. Form inputs should use `bg-gray-800 border-gray-700 text-white placeholder-gray-500` pattern common across Settings sub-tabs.

- **Loading/error state pattern**: Use `useState` for `loading` and `error`. Disable button + show spinner during `signInWithPassword()` call. Display `error.message` below form in a `text-red-400` block. Never expose raw stack traces — Supabase auth errors already return user-friendly messages like "Invalid login credentials".

- **Auth middleware is globally disabled** (CLAUDE.md gotcha): The backend auth middleware is intentionally commented out. This login page is for Supabase client-side auth, not the legacy `admin@rorca.local` JWT system. Ensure the Supabase session token is stored/managed by the auth context provider, not mixed with the old `POST /api/auth/login` flow.

- **Mobile-first**: Engineering standards require mobile-first design. Build the form layout for narrow viewports first (`max-w-sm mx-auto`), then scale. Test at 375px width minimum.

userStories.title: Build Register page with Supabase email+password signup
userStories.description:
Create src/pages/auth/RegisterPage.tsx. Calls supabase.auth.signUp(). Fields: email, password (min 8 chars), confirm password. Validate passwords match client-side. After signup show 'Check your email to confirm your account' if email confirmation is required; if auto-confirm (dev), navigate to /. Add route /auth/register in App.tsx.

## Context
- **Supabase auth pattern**: Use `supabase.auth.signUp({ email, password })` from the shared Supabase client instance. Check the response shape — `data.user` exists but `data.session` may be `null` when email confirmation is required (distinguish auto-confirm vs email-confirm by checking `data.session !== null`).
- **Route placement**: Add `/auth/register` in `App.tsx` **outside** any `RequireAuth` wrapper, alongside the login route. Follow existing react-router-dom v7 patterns already in the codebase (`<Route path="/auth/register" element={<RegisterPage />} />`).
- **Client-side validation**: Validate passwords match and `password.length >= 8` before calling `signUp()`. Display inline validation errors below each field — never rely solely on Supabase server errors for basic input validation (engineering standard: validate on both client and server).
- **Loading/error/empty states**: Disable the submit button and show a spinner during the signup request (engineering standard: handle loading, error, and empty states explicitly). Surface `error.message` from the Supabase response — never expose raw stack traces.
- **Navigation after signup**: Use `useNavigate()` from react-router-dom. On auto-confirm (session returned), navigate to `/`. On email confirmation required (no session), show the confirmation message and do NOT navigate — user must confirm email first.
- **Styling**: Use Tailwind utility classes only, mobile-first layout. Match the visual style of the existing LoginPage (if MU-005 is implemented first — this story depends on it). Use consistent form field components, spacing (`space-y-4`), and button styles.
- **Accessible markup**: Include `<label>` elements linked to inputs via `htmlFor`, use `type="email"` and `type="password"` on inputs, add `aria-describedby` for validation error messages, and use semantic `<form>` with `onSubmit` (not button `onClick`).
- **Link to login**: Place "Already have an account? Sign in" as a `<Link to="/auth/login">` below the form, consistent with the reverse link pattern on the login page.

userStories.title: Build ForgotPassword and ResetPassword pages
userStories.description:
Create src/pages/auth/ForgotPasswordPage.tsx (email input, calls supabase.auth.resetPasswordForEmail() with redirectTo pointing to /auth/reset-password) and src/pages/auth/ResetPasswordPage.tsx (new password form, detects access_token from URL hash, calls supabase.auth.updateUser()). Add both routes to App.tsx.

## Context
- **Supabase auth pattern**: Use `supabase.auth.resetPasswordForEmail()` and `supabase.auth.updateUser()` from the shared Supabase client instance. The `redirectTo` URL must use `window.location.origin` to work across localhost and deployed environments (Categoric VPS behind Tailscale at `100.91.193.49`).

userStories.title: Enable RLS on workspaces table with membership-based access policies
userStories.description:
Enable Row Level Security on the workspaces table and create policies using the get_user_workspace_ids() SECURITY DEFINER helper. Workers and schedulers use the Supabase service role key which bypasses all RLS policies. This is the foundation RLS story — all other workspace-scoped tables depend on workspaces being correctly secured first.

## Context
- **Migration format**: Use timestamp prefix `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_enable_rls_workspaces.sql` — sequential numbers (001–079) are legacy. The migration runner in `pg-index.ts` supports both formats; timestamps sort after sequential ones automatically.

- **Supabase RLS context**: This is a Supabase-native RLS migration, NOT the existing `pg` pool pattern. Policies use `auth.uid()` (Supabase's JWT-extracted user ID) and `get_user_workspace_ids()` (SECURITY DEFINER helper from MU-009). The service role key (`supabaseAdmin`) bypasses RLS entirely — no special policy needed for workers/schedulers.

- **Auth middleware is globally disabled**: Per CLAUDE.md, `authRequired` in `server.ts` is intentionally commented out (local single-user tool). RLS operates at the database level independently of Express middleware — this is the correct security boundary for Supabase-backed multi-user access.

- **Policy naming convention**: Prefix all policies with `workspace_` (e.g., `workspace_select_own`, `workspace_insert_authenticated`, `workspace_update_admin`, `workspace_delete_owner`). This matches the acceptance criteria and aids debugging in Supabase dashboard.

- **Existing table schema**: The `workspaces` table stores `id`, `label`, `path`, `domain` — check the actual column set in migrations before writing policies. The `workspace_members` table (or equivalent from MU-008/MU-009) provides the membership join; `get_user_workspace_ids()` encapsulates this lookup.

- **Foundation dependency**: This is the first RLS-enabled table — all other workspace-scoped tables (`pipeline_runs`, `story_results`, `wal_events`, `workspace_env_vars`, etc.) will chain their policies off `workspaces` access. Get the `SELECT` policy right; downstream tables will use `workspace_id IN (SELECT id FROM workspaces)` which implicitly inherits this RLS gate.

- **AGE search_path gotcha**: Any code using `setupAgeSession()` sets `search_path = ag_catalog` which exposes a different `workspaces` table (empty). RLS policies only apply to `rorca.workspaces` (the real table). The pool `on('connect')` guard in `db/index.ts` resets search_path, but verify RLS tests use the correct schema context.

- **Testing approach**: Use Supabase client with different JWT contexts (no JWT → 0 rows, user JWT → filtered rows, service role → all rows). The `anon` key should return 0 rows for unauthenticated access. Wrap tests in a transaction and rollback to avoid polluting state.

- **FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY — intentionally deferred**: The `rorca` DB user (used by the pg pool in `backend/src/db/index.ts`) is the table owner and bypasses RLS by default. `ALTER TABLE workspaces FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` would also subject the pool's `rorca` user to RLS, breaking all existing pool-based routes that haven't been migrated to `withUserClient()` yet. **Do NOT add FORCE RLS in this story** — the phased approach is: (1) enable RLS for direct Supabase client access (this story), (2) migrate all routes to `withUserClient()` (MU-022+), (3) add FORCE RLS in a dedicated hardening story after full migration. Document this in a comment in the migration.

- **Workspace membership join pattern**: For policies needing "workspace_id in user's workspaces", use a subquery like `workspace_id IN (SELECT workspace_id FROM team_members WHERE user_id = auth.uid())` or equivalent. - **Test with both service role and anon role**: RLS policies should allow full access for the service role (used by the backend pg pool) and restricted access for authenticated users. userStories.title: Configure PKCE flow and secure token storage
userStories.description:
Configure Supabase client to use PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) for all OAuth flows. Set flowType: 'pkce' in createClient() options. Verify tokens are stored in memory (Supabase SDK default) not localStorage. Document the security model: access_token in memory, automatic refresh via SDK.

## Context
- **Supabase client singleton**: Create `src/lib/supabase.ts` as a single `createClient()` export with `auth: { flowType: 'pkce', storage: undefined, persistSession: false }` to force in-memory-only token storage. The SDK's default `localStorage` adapter must be explicitly disabled — passing `storage: undefined` or a custom in-memory adapter prevents any persistence to `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`.

- **Environment variables**: Add `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` and `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` to `.env.example` with placeholder values. Per project conventions, never hardcode keys — use `import.meta.env.VITE_*` on the frontend. `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` goes in `backend/.env` (server-side only, not prefixed with `VITE_`).

- **PKCE flow is SDK-managed**: Supabase JS SDK v2+ handles `code_verifier`/`code_challenge` generation, temporary storage, and exchange automatically when `flowType: 'pkce'` is set. Do NOT implement PKCE manually — just configure the option and verify the `/auth/v1/token?grant_type=pkce` network request fires during OAuth callback.

- **Token refresh gotcha**: With `persistSession: false`, the SDK will NOT auto-refresh tokens across page reloads (no stored refresh_token to resume from). This is the correct security tradeoff for this story — document that sessions are ephemeral and require re-auth on full page reload. The `onAuthStateChange` listener handles in-session refresh transparently.

- **Verification approach for acceptance criteria**: The "no tokens in localStorage" check should be a manual DevTools verification documented in the PR description, not an automated test. For the in-memory storage assertion, a Vitest unit test can mock `createClient` and assert the config object shape.

- **Existing auth context**: Rorca has `src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx` — this story should NOT modify it yet (that's a separate migration story). The Supabase client created here will be consumed by future stories. Keep the module self-contained with just the client export and type re-exports from `@supabase/supabase-js`.

- **Security model documentation**: Add a brief comment block at the top of `supabase.ts` explaining: access_token held in JS memory only, no localStorage/sessionStorage/cookies, PKCE prevents auth code interception, XSS can read in-memory tokens but this is mitigated by CSP headers (separate concern). Keep it to 5-6 lines, not a README.

userStories.description:
Install helmet.js in backend and configure security headers on all responses. Add CSRF token generation and validation middleware for state-changing requests. ## Context
- **Helmet placement**: Apply `helmet()` in `server.ts` **before** all route mounts but **after** the CORS middleware and body parsers. The static serving path (`RORCA_SERVE_STATIC=1`) needs CSP to allow inline scripts for Vite dev mode — use `helmet.contentSecurityPolicy({ directives: { defaultSrc: ["'self'"], scriptSrc: ["'self'", "'unsafe-inline'"] } })` and tighten in production.
- **Auth is globally disabled**: `authRequired` middleware is intentionally commented out in `server.ts` (~line 78). CSRF tokens cannot be tied to authenticated sessions — use a double-submit cookie pattern instead (generate random token, set as `HttpOnly` cookie + return from `/api/auth/csrf-token`, validate cookie matches `X-CSRF-Token` header on mutating requests). This works without session state.
- **WebSocket security already exists**: The `/ws/terminal` endpoint in `server.ts` already has origin validation and short-lived connection tokens (OCT-021). CSRF middleware must **not** intercept WebSocket upgrade requests. Also exempt the SSE endpoints (`/api/pipeline/runs/:id/output`, `/api/pipeline/stream`) which use GET.
- **apiFetch.ts is the single HTTP client**: All frontend API calls go through `src/lib/apiFetch.ts`. Add CSRF token fetch on app init (or lazy on first mutating request), cache it in a module-level variable, and attach `X-CSRF-Token` header for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE. Handle 403 with `code: 'CSRF_INVALID'` by refetching token and retrying once.
- **Exempt paths must include MCP HTTP transport**: The CSRF exempt list should cover `/api/webhooks/*`, `/mcp/*`, `/api/health`, and also `/api/docs/*` (Swagger UI makes its own requests). MCP HTTP transport on `:3030/mcp` uses bearer token auth, not cookies — CSRF doesn't apply.
- **Helmet `X-Frame-Options: DENY`** is already set on WebSocket upgrade responses (OCT-021 security headers). Ensure helmet doesn't double-set or conflict — helmet's `frameguard` option will handle this globally, so remove the manual header from the WebSocket `verifyClient` if present.
- **Migration not needed**: This story is pure middleware + frontend changes — no new DB tables or columns. No migration file required.
- **CSP gotcha for xterm.js**: xterm.js uses inline styles and dynamic DOM manipulation. CSP `style-src` may need `'unsafe-inline'` to avoid breaking the terminal renderer. Test the RunTerminal component (`src/components/RunTerminal.tsx`) after enabling CSP.

userStories.title: Create getUserClient() for RLS-scoped DB queries in Express routes
userStories.description:
Create backend/src/db/user-client.ts providing getUserClient(req) that acquires a pool client and runs SET LOCAL request.jwt.claims to the authenticated user's JWT claims. This is how PostgreSQL RLS policies see auth.uid(). Add withUserClient(req, fn) convenience wrapper. Worker code (execution-engine.ts, worker.ts) explicitly continues using supabaseAdmin (service role) — document why.

## Context
- **Pool client pattern**: `backend/src/db/index.ts` manages the PostgreSQL Pool with max 20 connections, 30s idle timeout. `getUserClient()` must call `pool.connect()` from this shared pool — do NOT create a new Pool. Release is critical: always `client.release()` in `finally` to avoid connection leaks.

- **Auth middleware is globally disabled**: Per CLAUDE.md, `authRequired` is commented out in `server.ts`. `req.user` will be undefined in most requests. The `getUserClient()` guard (throw AuthError if `req.user` missing) is correct, but the 3 route updates must also have auth middleware enabled on those specific routes or the function will always throw. Check how `req.user` is populated — likely via a JWT-parsing middleware that needs to be applied per-route or globally re-enabled for RLS routes.

- **SET vs SET LOCAL**: Use `SET request.jwt.claims = $1` (session-level), NOT `SET LOCAL`. `SET LOCAL` only applies within an explicit transaction (BEGIN/COMMIT block) — in pg pool autocommit mode, `SET LOCAL` applies only to that single SET statement and is immediately gone. Session-level `SET` persists until `RESET` or connection close. **Critical**: always call `RESET request.jwt.claims` in the finally block before `client.release()` — otherwise the next request borrowing this pool connection inherits the previous user's claims, which is a data isolation vulnerability worse than no RLS at all.

- **AGE search_path gotcha**: If any of the 3 updated routes interact with Apache AGE graph queries, the `SET LOCAL request.jwt.claims` must not conflict with `setupAgeSession()` which sets `search_path = ag_catalog`. These are separate concerns but both use SET on the same client — ensure ordering is correct and search_path is restored.

- **Worker bypass documentation**: `worker.ts` and `execution-engine.ts` use `RORCA_PROCESS_ROLE=engine` env var to identify themselves. The comment explaining service-role bypass should reference this: worker processes run as the application service role (superuser/service key) because they execute on behalf of the system, not an individual user. Place comments at the `pool.connect()` call sites in both files.

- **Error class**: Use `AuthError` from `backend/src/lib/errors.ts` (part of the `AppError` hierarchy, maps to 401). Do not create a new error type.

- **TypeScript strict mode**: `PoolClient` type comes from `pg` package. The generic signature for `withUserClient<T>(req: Request, fn: (client: PoolClient) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>` must handle the case where `req.user` typing may not exist on Express's `Request` — check if there's an augmented type declaration in the project (likely in a `types/` or `@types/` directory).

- **Existing query helpers**: The codebase uses `queryOne<T>()`, `query<T>()`, `execute()` helpers from `db/index.ts` that use the pool directly. Routes updated to `withUserClient()` will bypass these helpers and use `client.query()` directly — this is expected but means those routes lose the helper's error formatting. Consider whether `withUserClient` should expose similar typed helpers on the scoped client.

userStories.description:
Systematically update the most important backend routes to use withUserClient() so RLS policies are enforced at the route level. Without this, routes still use the global pool and bypass RLS — data isolation is not enforced even with RLS enabled on tables. Prioritize: workspaces, pipeline runs, specs, direction.

## Context
- **`withUserClient()` pattern**: This is a new function introduced by the Supabase Auth + RLS spec (likely in `backend/src/db/index.ts` or a dedicated helper). It must acquire a client from the pool, run `SET LOCAL role = 'authenticated'; SET LOCAL request.jwt.claims = '<user JWT claims>'` (or equivalent `set_config` calls) so Postgres RLS policies activate, then return the client. Every route must `client.release()` in a `finally` block — connection leaks under RLS are worse than normal because the poisoned session carries stale role/claims.

- **AGE search_path interaction**: If any of these routes touch Apache AGE graph queries (knowledge graph features on workspaces), the `SET search_path = ag_catalog` from `setupAgeSession()` will conflict with RLS session variables. Ensure RLS session setup happens AFTER any AGE cleanup, or use separate clients. See `age_search_path_poison.md` for the prior pool-poisoning bug.

- **Route file locations**: Workspaces → `backend/src/routes/workspaces.ts`, Pipeline runs → `backend/src/routes/pipeline.ts`, Specs → `backend/src/routes/specs.ts`, Direction → `backend/src/routes/direction.ts`, Vault → `backend/src/routes/vault.ts`. Each has its own router; edits are scoped per file.

- **Auth middleware is globally disabled**: `authRequired` is commented out in `server.ts` (intentional for local dev). The RLS `withUserClient()` call needs the authenticated user's ID — it must come from `req.user` (populated by JWT middleware on individual routes) or a new per-route auth guard. userStories.title: Security audit: IDOR, RLS bypass, JWT manipulation, CSRF, XSS
userStories.description:
Perform a systematic security audit of the complete Supabase Auth + RLS implementation. Test for IDOR via API, RLS bypass attempts, JWT manipulation, CSRF bypass, XSS token theft, and rate limit bypass. Fix all HIGH/CRITICAL findings. Document results in security-audit.md.

## Context
- **Auth middleware is globally disabled** (`backend/src/server.ts` ~line 78, `authRequired` commented out). This story is part of the Supabase Auth migration (MU-029), so the new Supabase auth middleware must be in place and enforced on all protected routes before these tests are meaningful. Verify the middleware chain is active before auditing.

- **RLS context depends on `withUserClient()`**: Supabase RLS enforcement requires per-request client instantiation with the user's JWT (`SET request.jwt.claims`). Confirm every route that touches RLS-protected tables (especially `vault_keys`, `workspaces`, `workspace_env_vars`, `budget_config`) uses `withUserClient()` and not the service-role pool (`pool` from `db/index.ts`), which bypasses RLS entirely.

- **AGE search_path pool poison is a related attack surface**: `setupAgeSession()` sets `search_path = ag_catalog` on pool connections. If graph queries don't restore the search path, a subsequent request could hit `ag_catalog.workspaces` (empty) instead of `rorca.workspaces`, potentially leaking incorrect 404s that reveal table existence. Audit graph code paths for proper cleanup in `knowledge-graph.ts`, `graph-context.ts`, `graph-drift-detector.ts`.

- **Rate limiter has known bypass in test mode**: `rate-limiter.ts` is skipped when `NODE_ENV=test` unless `RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=true`. Ensure the audit runs with rate limiting active. Default limits: 100 req/min authenticated, 20 req/min unauthenticated, keyed by `userId:method:path` or `ip:method:path`.

- **No sensitive data in error responses**: `errors.ts` has an `AppError` hierarchy that serializes to `{ error, code, details }`. Audit that no route handler catches errors and returns raw `err.message` (which could contain SQL, JWT fragments, or stack traces). Especially check `try/catch` blocks in `backend/src/routes/` that don't use the `AppError` subclasses.

- **CSRF protection must be newly implemented**: The existing codebase has no CSRF middleware (local single-user tool historically). The Supabase Auth migration introduces multi-user, so CSRF tokens (`X-CSRF-Token` header or double-submit cookie) need to be added to all state-changing endpoints (`POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`). This is new infrastructure, not just an audit of existing code.

- **Token storage audit — check both paths**: Frontend auth tokens may be stored in `localStorage` (XSS-vulnerable) or `httpOnly` cookies (secure). Check `src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx` and any `apiFetch` interceptors in `src/lib/` for where Supabase session tokens are persisted. The acceptance criteria require no tokens in `localStorage` — confirm `httpOnly` cookie or in-memory-only storage is used.

- **WebSocket endpoint is a high-value IDOR target**: `/ws/terminal` already has origin validation and one-time `wsToken` auth (see CLAUDE.md WebSocket Security Model). Verify that the Supabase Auth migration didn't regress these guards — especially that `wsToken` generation now requires a valid Supabase session, not just any unauthenticated `POST /api/terminal/sessions`.
